name: Question 6
problem:
Find the solution of the initial value problem

$$
{x}^{2}{y}^{″}-9x{y}^{′}+25y=0,\,y(1)=-2,\,{y}^{′}(1)=4,\,x>0.
$$
worked_solution:
The given equation is an instance of the Cauchy-Euler equation. So, we assume that the solutions take the form $y={x}^{\lambda }.$ Differentiating $y$ with respect to $x$ gives

$$
{y}^{′}=\lambda {x}^{\lambda -1},\,{y}^{″}=\lambda (\lambda -1){x}^{\lambda -2}.
$$

Substituting the above to our differential equation gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}\cdot \lambda (\lambda -1){x}^{\lambda -2}-9x\cdot \lambda {x}^{\lambda -1}+25{x}^{\lambda } & =0 \\ \lambda (\lambda -1){x}^{\lambda }-9\lambda {x}^{\lambda }+25{x}^{\lambda } & =0 \\ {x}^{\lambda }[\lambda (\lambda -1)-9\lambda +25] & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the auxiliary equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}\lambda (\lambda -1)-9\lambda +25 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}-10\lambda +25 & =0 \\ (\lambda -5)^{2} & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we have a double root $\lambda =5.$
Therefore, the general solution is

$$
y(x)={c}_{1}{x}^{5}+{c}_{2}{x}^{5}\operatorname{ln}⁡x.
$$

Now let's find the constants ${c}_{1}$ and ${c}_{2}.$

Substituting $y(1)=-2$ into the general solution gives

$$
-2={c}_{1}.
$$

We now need to apply the condition ${y}^{′}(1)=4.$ First, we differentiate $y$ to find ${y}^{′}$:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =5{x}^{4}{c}_{1}+{c}_{2}{x}^{4}+5{c}_{2}{x}^{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting ${y}^{′}(1)=4$ and ${c}_{1}=-2$ into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}4 & =5{c}_{1}+{c}_{2} \\ 4 & =-10+{c}_{2} \\ {c}_{2} & =14.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the initial value problem is

$$
\begin{aligned}y(x) & =-2{x}^{5}+14{x}^{5}\operatorname{ln}⁡x \\  & =2{x}^{5}(7\operatorname{ln}⁡x-1).\end{aligned}
$$

Question 6
?

Find the solution of the initial value problem x2y″−9xy′+25y=0,y(1)=−2,y′(1)=4,x>0.

a
y(x)=2x5(ln⁡x+1)
b
y(x)=2x5(ln⁡x+2)
c
y(x)=x−5(7ln⁡x−2)
d
y(x)=2x5(7ln⁡x−1)
e
y(x)=x−5(ln⁡x−1)
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The given equation is an instance of the Cauchy-Euler equation. So, we assume that the solutions take the form y=xλ. Differentiating y with respect to x gives

y′=λxλ−1,y″=λ(λ−1)xλ−2.

Substituting the above to our differential equation gives

x2⋅λ(λ−1)xλ−2−9x⋅λxλ−1+25xλ=0λ(λ−1)xλ−9λxλ+25xλ=0xλ[λ(λ−1)−9λ+25]=0.

Therefore, the auxiliary equation is

λ(λ−1)−9λ+25=0λ2−10λ+25=0(λ−5)2=0.

Hence, we have a double root λ=5. Therefore, the general solution is y(x)=c1x5+c2x5ln⁡x.

Now let's find the constants c1 and c2.

Substituting y(1)=−2 into the general solution gives −2=c1.

We now need to apply the condition y′(1)=4. First, we differentiate y to find y′: y′=5x4c1+c2x4+5c2x4ln⁡x

Substituting y′(1)=4 and c1=−2 into the above gives 4=5c1+c24=−10+c2c2=14.

Therefore, the solution to the initial value problem is y(x)=−2x5+14x5ln⁡x=2x5(7ln⁡x−1).
